Why the effective rate jumps at £100,000. Between £100,000 and £125,140 you lose £1 of Personal Allowance for every £2 of extra pay, so the rate on your next pound is about 62% including NI.

Frequently asked questions

What are the UK tax brackets for 2026/27?

In England, Wales and Northern Ireland: 0% up to £12,570, 20% to £50,270, 40% to £125,140, and 45% above. Scotland has six bands from 19% to 48%.

Do I pay the higher rate on all my income if I earn over £50,270?

No. Only the part above £50,270 is taxed at 40%. Someone on £60,000 pays 20% on the first £37,700 of taxable income and 40% only on the remaining £9,730.

Have the thresholds changed?

The main thresholds (£12,570 allowance and £50,270 higher-rate threshold) are unchanged from 2025/26. The Government has said they stay frozen until April 2031, which pulls more people into higher rates as pay rises. Scottish thresholds do change.

Are Welsh tax rates different?

Wales can set its own rates but they currently match England.

Where can I check official rates?

See GOV.UK's "Income Tax rates and Personal Allowances" page and gov.scot for Scottish Income Tax. Our methodology lists our sources.
